GHA.note: Nothing on the central bank's payments role.
Nothing on digital financial consumer protection.
Only says Ghana is working with the AfCFTA Secretariat on cross-border payment systems; no corridor piloted, licensed or in service.

facts.fact: The Labari Journal, citing IMANI Africa, names a Cybersecurity Authority among Ghana's existing regulators, responsible for breach protocols.

GHA.note: Says only that Ghana has no comprehensive legal framework for data centres and cloud; no data centre named.

facts.fact: The Labari Journal reports critics at IMANI Africa saying Section 31 of the NITA Bill, before Parliament and not passed, 'appears to' enable a requirement to store operational data on government-managed local servers.

GHA.note: Data Protection Commission is mentioned only as a regulator for localisation rules; no law, appointment or ruling stated.
No statement about the data protection law itself.
The local-server provision concerns operators' data, not state data; nothing on state data rules.
The minister's four-pillar agenda is framed around bills, with no national digital strategy named.
Nothing on government payments to people.

facts.fact: The Labari Journal says the Data Harmonisation Bill, developed by NITA and before Ghana's Parliament, would set a legal framework for data sharing and make it mandatory for all public institutions to integrate their systems under uniform data standards; it has not passed.

GHA.note: Mentions foreign venture capital only as a bill's effect; no finance stated.
Article says the bills would contradict the AfCFTA digital trade protocol; no signature, ratification or national law giving effect stated.
Hosting the AfCFTA Secretariat and working with it on digital trade protocols is stated in general terms; no dated agreement or digital-policy body membership.
Nothing on mobile money or retail payments.
Nothing on electronic payment of taxes or fees.

facts.fact: The Labari Journal lists the Ghana Innovation and Startup Bill among 15 ICT-related bills to be laid before or being considered by Ghana's Parliament, with no confirmation they will pass.
